newsitem.title: POLAND: Floods may make little mark on Poland grain crop.
newsitem.headline: Floods may make little mark on Poland grain crop.

text.p: Poland's grain output may be reduced slightly by recent flooding in wheat-rich south-western regions, but losses will be contained if the rains stop soon, analysts said on Tuesday.
Analysts had forecast this year's grain output to be roughly equal to or just below the 24.7 million tonnes produced in 1996, with estimates ranging from about 23.5-25 million tonnes.

"It seems that forecasts of the grain harvest falling some two to three percent are realistic, with much larger falls in output not probable despite all this rain," Andrzej Kalicki, analyst at the Warsaw Commodities Exchange, told Reuters.
However, analysts said output might be reduced significantly if rains persisted and flooding continued,

"Flooding will cause losses in the south-west, but it is too early to put an exact figure on it," said an analyst, adding that losses should amount to less than five percent if weather patterns returned to normal.
A spokesman for the agriculture ministry told Reuters that no official crop loss estimates would be given until water levels dropped and fields were examined, which could take days.
Over the past fews days heavy downpours have resulted in flooding in many parts of southern Poland.
